methodological_rigor.justification: Translational molecular correlative study of 30 patients with FGFR2-driven tumors from phase I/II ReFocus trial (NCT04526106) and UNLOCK-03 program at Gustave Roussy, integrating ctDNA (Foundation Medicine, Illumina, IntegraGen panels), tissue WES (140x coverage), bulk RNA-seq, Ba/F3 cell models with site-directed mutagenesis, Western blot signaling analysis, PDX models (3 independent), and structural analysis (PyMOL superimposition, Maestro mutation modeling). Statistical comparisons use DESeq2 with BH-adjusted FDR<0.01 and NES threshold, and exact permutation test for mutation spectrum comparison (P<1×10^-5). IC50 fold-change quantification and in vivo efficacy measurement rigorous. Cohort size (n=30) is a limitation for subgroup analyses.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Translational correlative study of a prospective phase I/II clinical trial (ReFocus) combined with institutional molecular programs - Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is exceptionally high: provides immediately actionable treatment sequencing guidance (lirafugratinib followed by futibatinib, or vice versa) based on precise resistance mutations, demonstrated in 3 patients who experienced prolonged response to futibatinib after lirafugratinib progression. Directly informs precision oncology practice for FGFR2-driven cholangiocarcinoma and other rare tumor types with approved/emerging FGFR2 inhibitors.

reporting_quality.justification: Ethics approval documented (French ANSM; animal APAFIS#2790-2015112015055793 and APAFIS#2328-2015101914074846); clinical trial IDs (NCT04526106, NCT04932525, NCT02517892) reported; FGFR2 residue numbering conventions explicitly clarified (NM_001144913.1 vs NM_000141.4). Molecular platforms and VAF thresholds disclosed. RRID identifiers used for software. Supplementary tables/figures referenced for detailed mutation spectra. Data source for comparator cohort (Goyal et al. 2024 Table 3, Fig 4, Supp Fig S3F) explicitly cited.

novelty_literature.justification: First comprehensive characterization of lirafugratinib resistance mutations in a clinical cohort, identifying an unprecedented enrichment at FGFR2 M538 and L618 residues (69% of acquired resistance cases). The head-to-head comparison with futibatinib resistance spectrum reveals complementary mutational profiles supporting a novel treatment sequencing strategy. The finding is mechanistically grounded (structural analysis, Ba/F3 IC50 data, PDX in vivo efficacy) and clinically validated in 3 patients. Represents a paradigm contribution to FGFR2 precision oncology.

writing_presentation.justification: Exceptionally clear manuscript with logical structure moving from cohort description through primary/acquired resistance categorization, through complementary activity of the two inhibitors, to structural mechanistic basis, to clinical validation. Figures and schematics communicate complex mutation spectra and sequencing strategies effectively. Specific attention to technical details (FGFR2 residue numbering conventions) reflects scholarly care.

key_strengths: First systematic characterization of lirafugratinib resistance spectrum with unprecedented M538/L618 mutation enrichment (69% of acquired resistance cases)
Head-to-head comparison with futibatinib resistance data from Goyal et al. 2024 (statistical permutation test P < 1×10^-5) revealing complementary mutational profiles
Multi-layered mechanistic validation: Ba/F3 IC50 fold-changes, Western blot downstream signaling, PDX in vivo efficacy, and PyMOL/Maestro structural modeling of binding interactions
Clinical validation: 3 patients with lirafugratinib progression experienced prolonged response to subsequent futibatinib, demonstrating direct translational utility
Leverages prospective trial cohort (NCT04526106 ReFocus) with comprehensive ctDNA, WES, and RNA-seq molecular profiling
key_concerns: Cohort size (n=30, 16 with acquired resistance) is modest, limiting statistical power for subtype-specific analyses
Three-patient post-lirafugratinib futibatinib validation cohort is small; larger prospective trial would strengthen the sequencing recommendation
Some novel FGFR2 mutations (G584R, L611V, K660S/T, G664E) found only once, limiting robust conclusions about their functional significance
chief_reviewer.rationale: Translational precision oncology study with immediate clinical actionability, rigorous multi-modal mechanistic validation, and paradigm-defining sequential treatment strategy, fitting Tier 1 (JCO / Cancer Discovery / Nature Cancer-caliber) with minor revisions.
